searchText: tbh I am not that worried about jumpdest; am more worried about the size of data that needs to be read from disk in only a couple seconds Jumpdest can now do more or less at speed of RAM Even NVMe going to struggle if at the top end we need to load 8GB, 16GB, 32GB etc per block So code loading will become the new gaslimit cap; which would be unfortunate when its only in these niche attack scenarios I think we are ok for Glamsterdam? > Meter Contract Code Size, but not increase limit. We already did the increase limit bit 🙂 Exactly, so it should be removed from EIP-7907 🙂 Sure 🙂 Making PR https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12398 RE: gas cap, I will let Maria weigh in but you could indeed be correct that this is the constraint. We can calculate how much bytes are read at most (theoretical max) which is `(block_gas_limit // COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS) * MAX_CODE_SIZE`, which for 200 Mgas is (for Glamsterdam) `4166.625` MiB (`~4.069 GiB`) I am getting confused by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7870 If `Random 4K Read IOPS: At least ~50,000` isn't this off by a lot? Isn't this `(4096 * 50_000) / (1024 * 1024)` is 195 MiB/s? Also this: `Sequential R/W: At least ~500 MB/s` Am I missing something here? 🤔 Note that also with current max size (which is `3/8` of Glamsterdam) this then still looks problematic I am not an author of this EIP BTW, so you should check with them 🙂 Done Heh this is fast If an EIP badge for this would exist (you are not author but get changes quickly merged) then this PR is def. a candidate for it haha (Quickdraw badge) Boom, its done https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7907

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
RE: gas cap, I will let Maria weigh in but you could indeed be correct that this is the constraint. We can calculate how much bytes are read at most (theoretical max) which is `(block_gas_limit // COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS) * MAX_CODE_SIZE`, which for 200 Mgas is (for Glamsterdam) `4166.625` MiB (`~4.069 GiB`)

I am getting confused by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7870
If `Random 4K Read IOPS: At least ~50,000` isn't this off by a lot? Isn't this `(4096 * 50_000) / (1024 * 1024)` is 195 MiB/s?
Also this: `Sequential R/W: At least ~500 MB/s`

Am I missing something here? 🤔  Note that also with current max size (which is `3/8` of Glamsterdam) this then still looks problematic
